messages.author: 4c9160a813adaffc
messages.subject: Re: Problem in installing Rhipe and R
parts:
I removed rhlapply. I should update the docs. The effect of rhlapply
can be replicated

given rhlapply(1:N, F) i.e compute F(i) for i=1,..N

M = expression({
   F=function(....){

   }
  lapply(map.values,function(r){
           rhcollect(r, F(r) )
})
})

z=rhmr(map=M, N=N,
inout=c("lapply","seq"),ofolder="/tmp/outputfolder",mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0))
rhex(z)


It is wordy, but it is boilerplate and you can replace it using
quote/bquote/substitute and R's lisp style macro functions

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Problem in installing Rhipe and R
parts:
This was my response. I should point running rhcollect for i in 1:N is
not needed.
E.g. if F(i) is a real number and the trial id is not important, you could

rhcollect(1, unlist(lapply(map.values, F)) )

the 1 is just dummy. When this data is read back, you'll get

[1]
[[1]] 1
[[2]] F(1) F(2) .....

[2]]
[[1]] 1
[[2]] F(100) F(101) ....

This is very useful if you have millions of trials. Reading in
millions of keys,values (as would be the case if one follows the
example below)
would take very long time.

If the trial # is needed, you could do
rhcollect(1,
do.call("rbind", lapply(map.values,function(r){
c( r, F(r) )})) )

Some tips to make your experience better.

Saptarshi
